page: Microsoft Azure F32als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The server does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying on remote network-attached premium storage for persistent data operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, driven by full non-hyperthreaded physical cores. The instance scored 21,770.0 in multi-core Geekbench, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, alongside a strong single-core score of 2,101.0. Stress-ng returned 98,523.95 points in multi-core operations, while PassMark delivered a CPU score of 62,597.18 and extended instructions test rating of 77,524.29. Memory bandwidth testing logged 4,749.4 GB/sec on cached small blocks and 155.08 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. For inference evaluations, small language models reached 4,505.54 prompt tokens per second, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 412.39 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is focused around raw CPU processing cycles per dollar rather than RAM or persistent local drive capacity. By providing dedicated physical execution cores without SMT concurrency contention, the instance maximizes per-thread compute density. The absence of local disk drives avoids paying for unneeded ephemeral hardware, though applications requiring extensive persistent local storage must account for external storage volume overhead.

The hardware profile and performance profile suit compute-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Primary target workloads include software compilation, video and batch image processing, scientific modeling, CPU-bound web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and mathematical physics simulations.
